A security-wide search for smartcard/vault/credential/NGC object names, service names and process names returned 0 hits, and the windows.other check for scardsvr/vaultsvc service installs or image paths also returned 0 hits. The only LSASS handle events with unusual access masks were: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976) on scranton.dmevals.local opening lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff at 2020-05-02T03:05:16, plus routine system readers (svchost.exe via lsm.dll/sysmain.dll, csrss.exe, wininit.exe, wsmprovhost.exe). The PowerShell LSASS access occurred in the same session where user pbeesly was running a credential/certificate collection toolkit from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1 (Get-PrivateKeys exporting cert:\LocalMachine certificates to .pfx with Export-PfxCertificate, Invoke-Discovery, Invoke-Persistence, Invoke-Exfil, sdelete64 wiping of C:\programdata\victim\???cod.3aka3.scr and Draft.Zip). That is credential/certificate theft (T1552/T1555/T1649 territory), not MFA interception: no smartcard reader, no vault, no MFA token or OTP interception artefact was retrieved. The 4648 explicit-credential logons for pbeesly (scranton -> NASHUA, and PSEXESVC.exe on nashua) and the Kerberos KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED failures from 10.0.1.4/10.0.1.6 in the non-overlapping zeek window are consistent with normal pre-auth negotiation and lateral use of harvested credentials, not with intercepted MFA.
